correctness.rationale: The exact distance-two adjacency lists are exhaustively obtained from length-at-most-two walks. The five index regimes comprise all v_i deletion stages for every n>=13; each displayed closed-neighborhood fold is checked by finite symbolic offset comparisons, leaving one link vertex. Dominated vertices collapse their flag complexes, and a vertex with collapsible link can itself be removed by simplicial collapse. The remaining C_n^2 has only consecutive-triple 2-faces, with each chord a free edge, and collapses to C_n. At n=12, exact F2 boundary ranks (1,23,85,72,12) from simplex counts (24,108,160,84,12) give reduced H2 rank 3 and all other reduced ranks zero. The standalone standard-library checker builds original edges and recomputes distances, 742 link fold checks over n=13..40, and exact full n=12 homology; these finite tests support but do not replace the parameter-uniform fold proof. The result concerns only inclusive scale two and integer n>=13, plus the finite n=12 F2 boundary.

originality.rationale: The explicit all-n inner-vertex simplicial collapse and the exact n=12 obstruction are not implied by the nearest full-text graph-square and circle-Rips papers. Adamaszek (arXiv:1104.0433) requires girth at least seven for Proposition 2.2 and has additional alternative hypotheses failing on the cubic graphs GP(n,2), which possess square-graph five-cliques. Its cycle classification covers only the final outer ring after the new reduction. Adamaszek–Adams (arXiv:1503.03669) treats metric circles and cyclic graphs rather than the two-ring metric. Scientific alias/fingerprint searches and examination of closest indexed titles identified no covering theorem, but undiscovered earlier treatments remain possible.

value.rationale: Generalized Petersen graphs form a canonical two-ring infinite cubic family, and the five-cycles force the failure of the natural girth-seven graph-square collapse criterion. Nonetheless explicit link dismantling yields a strong simplicial-collapse theorem for all n>=13. The exact three-dimensional F2 H2 at n=12 supplies a sharp homological obstruction to moving the stable collapse threshold one step earlier. This structural regime transition is motivated by an identified gap in graph-power topology, not a purely numerical extrapolation or an arbitrary finite example.
